section: Department of Justice divisions and schemes
content: Department of Justice dashboard lists centrally sponsored schemes and judicial-reform work, including eCourts, Fast Track Special Courts, Fast Track Courts, Family Courts, Gram Nyayalayas, MP/MLA Special Courts, NALSA, and judicial-officer vacancy information. For current dashboards, use the official Department of Justice dashboard.

Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), including exclusive POCSO Courts, are reported on the Department of Justice dashboard. The dashboard states that setting up and functioning of FTSCs is within the domain of State Governments in consultation with their respective High Courts. It also states that the information is as reported by the concerned High Courts. Use the official dashboard for current court, disposal, pendency, and fund figures.

The official eCourts single-sign-on portal provides ePay, eFiling Services, High Court NJDG, District Court NJDG, judgment search, High Court and District Court services, and the eCourts Services mobile app. NJDG is described as a monitoring tool to identify, manage and reduce case pendency. eFiling Services are described as online filing of cases enabled by digital tools. Use the relevant official service link from the eCourts portal rather than relying on a chatbot for a live case result.

The official eFiling platform is an end-to-end solution for online filing of plaints, written statements, replies, and applications. It states that civil and criminal cases can be filed before High Courts, District Courts, or Taluka Courts in India. Listed facilities include drafting templates, online vakalat submission, eSign for uploaded documents, online court-fee payment through relevant State treasury gateways, online oath video recording, and a case portfolio. Availability and filing requirements can vary by court; confirm requirements on the portal for the selected court.

Procedure: 1. Open the official eFiling portal. 2. Select the relevant court and complete the portal’s registration and verification steps. 3. Prepare and upload the documents required by that court. 4. Review the filing and use the portal’s payment option where applicable. 5. Submit and check the portal for acknowledgement or subsequent status.

ePay is the official online payment platform of the eCourts Project, developed, hosted and maintained by NIC under guidance of the e-Committee of the Supreme Court of India. It supports court-related payments such as court fees, judicial deposits, fines, penalties, and other dues. The exact payment types and workflow depend on the selected court and service. Use only the official ePay site and review the payment details before completing a transaction.

The eCourts Services Mobile App is an official digital platform for case-related information, orders, judgments, and court services for High Courts and District Courts. It is available from the Google Play Store and Apple App Store and is free to use. The FAQ says registration is not required to use the app. It offers Quick Links to ePay, eFiling, NJDG, judgment search, and Virtual Courts. It supports English and regional languages including Hindi.

To search by CNR in the app: 1. Enter the 16-character alphanumeric CNR without spaces or hyphens. 2. Select Search. 3. Review the displayed case history, case details, case status, hearing history, and orders. If CNR is unavailable, use the alternative supported search options.

The official Tele-Law FAQ says Tele-Law uses video conferencing and telephone services to connect people who need legal advice with lawyers, through Common Service Centres at Gram Panchayat level. The service is free of cost for citizens. A person can approach a CSC or register through the Tele-Law citizen mobile application to seek legal advice. The FAQ states that the mobile app can be downloaded from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store. Use the official Tele-Law portal to find current CSC and appointment details.

A Department of Justice Lok Sabha reply describes eCourts work including e-filing, e-payments, video conferencing, Virtual Courts and live streaming. It reports that live streaming of court proceedings was operational in 11 High Courts as of 31 January 2026. Streaming availability, the matters covered, and access links can change; use the official website of the relevant court. The same official DoJ material refers to online filing and digital payment services under eCourts. For Tele-Law information and access, use the Department of Justice’s official Tele-Law service pages or portal rather than relying on case-specific advice.
